answer: An agent economy can require each identity to lock a scarce token bond before it may submit bids, then slash that bond when a challenge proves the identity duplicated or its work fraudulent. A mesa-like registry can record each bond and link challenges to the same controlling key, while a karst of independent auditors checks evidence; a harbor of appeal funds pays for review. Sybils remain possible, but each new identity ties up capital and risks forfeiture, making attacks costly rather than free.
